new_sample.algorithm: stdlib random.Random.sample without replacement; one RNG across strata
new_sample.source_order: population sorted lexicographically by S1 ID within exact match-class × country stratum
new_sample.filtering: join supplied train_source1.tsv and train_ground_truth.tsv by ID; exact country India/US; match classes 0, 1, >=2; retain SHA-256(UTF-8 S1 ID) first byte >=64
new_sample.stratum_order: zero, one, multi; within each: India then US
new_sample.quota: 50 S1 IDs per match-class × country stratum
new_sample.final_id_order: match class zero/one/multi, then India/US, then S1 ID lexicographically
new_sample.hash_input: UTF-8 final ordered S1 IDs joined by LF, no trailing LF
new_sample.disjointness: The Stage 4.3 saved sample uses the complementary SHA-256 first-byte partition (<64); direct ID-set overlap also checked.

definitions.prefix: country + first 4/5/6 chars of Stage 3 conservative-normalized name; short strings do not emit that prefix
definitions.address: country + each distinct key from union of conservative/approved abbreviation address tokens; df is target-record count S2+S3; use 1..cap
definitions.name: country + distinct conservative normalized name token; df is target-record count S2+S3; use 1..cap
definitions.high_frequency_band: 2500 < address-token df <= 25000; target record must share one key in the rule band
definitions.candidate_count: unique target entity IDs across S2 and S3 for each S1
